definitions.series_a: Series A (headline): daily return on capital deployed. r_A(t) = sum_i V_i(t-1) r_i(t) / sum_i V_i(t-1) over copied lots held into day t (bought before t, sold on or after t); V = units x adjusted close, so returns include dividends. A lot bought on day t earns from t+1; a lot sold on day t earns day t's return, then leaves. Days with no open lot earn the Ken French daily risk-free rate.
definitions.series_b: Series B (fixed pot): one pot K = the warm-up book at market value at the start of the window (L2) plus C0 = peak cumulative net cash invested over the measurement period (purchases minus sale proceeds). The cash earns the risk-free rate; purchases draw it down, sale proceeds refill it. r_B(t) = NAV(t)/NAV(t-1) - 1 with NAV = cash + value of open lots.
definitions.event_panel:
Trade-level panel for the Phase 5 event study (D14, D16).

One row per in-scope PURCHASE and SALE record whose entry date falls in the sample (whether or not the
copier could act on it: an ignored sale is still a signal). Prices are adjusted closes (total return).
  r_entry_h   return from the close on the ENTRY date to the close h NYSE trading days later (the copier)
  r_txn_h     the same from the close on the TRANSACTION date (what the senator earned); a transaction
              date that is not a trading day uses the first trading day on or after it
  gap         return from the transaction-date close to the entry-date close: what the disclosure lag
              costs a copier
  x_*         the same minus SPY's return over exactly the same days (simple difference)
A horizon that runs past the last day of the sample is censored (blank); N per horizon is reported. If a
symbol's series ends before the horizon, its last close is carried forward (flag series_ended_in_horizon).
Records with no price on the start date are left blank (flag no_price).
definitions.book_rules:
The position book: FIFO lots per (senator, price symbol), built from the events day by day.

Rules (Phase 4 brief, D12, A03, E20/K1, J3, K3):
  Purchase        open a lot: dollars = the event's size, units = dollars / adjusted close on the entry
                  date. Adjusted closes include dividends, so every lot is a total-return position.
  Sale (Full)     close every open lot of that senator in that price symbol, regardless of owner.
  Sale (Partial)  sell units worth the event's size at that day's adjusted close, oldest lot first,
                  capped at what is held.
  Nothing held    a sale is ignored and logged (no shorting; this includes anything bought before the book
                  starts: 12 months before the window with the warm-up (L2), the window's first day under V17).
  Reversal (J3)   a correction first undoes its predecessor's copied action: a purchase's lots still open
                  are sold ("reversal"); a sale's units are bought back as a new lot. Then the correction
                  acts itself if it is in scope.
  No price        a purchase needs an adjusted close on its exact entry date (E24). A symbol with no
                  usable history at all is in the survivorship ledger: skipped and logged (K3), or, with
                  engine.ledger_trades: spy_fill (V15), held as a lot that is valued with SPY. A symbol
                  with a history but no print that day is skipped and logged. A sale of a held symbol on
                  a day without a print uses the last available close (flagged).
  Series ends     a lot whose price series ends before the last day closes at the last available adjusted
                  close on that day ("series ended", E20).
  Last day        lots still open are marked at that day's close ("end of window").
Same-day order: the events' order (see events.py). Series that end are closed after the day's events.

Lots are written as PIECES: a partial sale splits a lot into a closed piece and the remainder, so every row
of lots.csv has one entry and one exit; entry dollars are split pro rata by units.
definitions.events:
Events: one row per record the copier acts on (or reverses), with its entry date and size.

Headline (J3, as first published): every in-scope record of data/processed/trade_records.csv acts on its
entry date. A record that corrects an earlier one (record_no > 1) first REVERSES its predecessor's copied
action, if there was one, and then acts itself if it is in scope; so an out-of-scope correction whose
predecessor was in scope is kept as a reversal-only event. V14 ("as revised", data.amendment_values:
as_revised) uses trades_clean.csv instead: one record per trade, corrected values, first datetime.

Entry date (D11, trades.price_timing):
  next_close_after_disclosure  the first NYSE trading day strictly AFTER the disclosure date (headline)
  same_day_close               V9: the disclosure date itself when the filing is timestamped before
                               trades.same_day_cutoff_et on a trading day; otherwise as the headline
Same-day ordering (logged in DECISIONS.md, E29): entry date, then disclosure datetime, then transaction
date, then row number in the input file.
Size (trades.sizing): midpoint (amount_mid; the open top band uses its lower bound, D10) | lower_bound |
equal_dollar (trades.equal_dollar_amount).
